html:
Hopitutskwa is the Hopi name for their land, on and around three mesas in northeast Arizona. Today the Hopi Reservation lies at its heart, surrounded entirely by the Navajo Nation.

The Hopi are Pueblo people who descend from the Ancestral Puebloans. They farm maize, beans and squash in a dry land using careful dry-farming, and hold a cycle of ceremonies, including katsina dances. The village of Oraibi, founded around 1100, is one of the oldest continuously lived-in places in the United States.

Spanish friars came in 1629. The Hopi joined the Pueblo Revolt of 1680, killed the friars and never let the missions return. In 1882 the US set up a reservation for them, and long land disputes with the Navajo followed. Their Pueblo kin to the east are the Zuni.
